chapter: Bucktown, Chicago and the cabaret years
title: From Bucktown to Chicago: King Oliver at the Dreamland and other cabarets
summary: She came to like cabaret work and went to Chicago, where she joined King Oliver's band at the Dreamland. She then worked briefly at Freddie Keppard's place and with Glover Compton at the De Luxe.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: That's the first time I met Manuel then, out there. And so then I stayed there and I worked a while and I got the idea then that I liked it. Because I didn't like Cabaret Week. Before when I was working in the theaters and on the carnival shows and things, every city that I would be near or I played into, I would go, like at night, going out stepping, and I'd go to a cabaret. Well, as soon as they knew that I was singing, they'd ask me to do a number, they'd offer me a job. But, ooh, I didn't like that. I didn't like that close contact with the people. You could hear everything they said, all the remarks they would make, and I said, no, I wouldn't work. And when I was in Chicago, Tony Jackson, a great piano player from here, he was playing at the Teen Ann Jones'. I think they called it the Eli Number One. And so he introduced me to Teen Ann Jones. I've got the rose still that he gave me after I got through singing. I've got the petals in a Bible, you know. He gave it to me and I put it in a Bible and I still got it. After I got through singing and they offered me a job, but I didn't like it. I didn't want no cabaret work. I didn't like it. But then after I worked in Bucktown and they treated me so nice and I made so much money, they used to just throw five dollars out there. Well, that was the time, you know, the Storyville was going full blast then. So all of the people from there used to come out after hours, you know. And I made plenty of money out there. So that made me like it. Well, then I went to Chicago. And I arrived in Chicago on, I think it was a Tuesday night. And that Wednesday night we went out cabaret and our first place was, I wanted to go where King Oliver was playing. And that was the dreamland. And we went there. And as soon as King saw me, well, right away he requested a song. And I said, oh, I don't know what to sing. He said, well, come on. Ain't nobody around here singing Sister Kate. Come on and sing Sister Kate. And so I got out there and I said, and there was a little midget selling cigars and cigarettes. And I said, I'm not going to do no shimmying, though I'll sing the song. But I ain't going to shimmy like Sister Kate. And he says, well, I'll shimmy for you. And there I was out there singing the little midget was doing the shimmying. And so then I got a job that night. They hired me that night. And I stayed there and I worked with King. Well, he had Louis Armstrong was playing carnet. And Lil was playing. That was before he married Lil. Lil Harding, her name was then. She was at the piano. I think Dodds, I think Baby Dodds was playing drums. I think Eddie Garland was on the bass. Eddie Garland was on bass. Well, anyway, that's a bunch. Well, I stayed there and work. And then when I left there, I went Freddie Keper after me to come work at the entertainers. That was on 35th Street, Izzy Shaw's place, black and tan. And I went there. But I had a kind of a hard gang to buck up against there. They were mostly all dancers, you see, no singers. And so naturally, he wanted somebody who could sing, you see. And usually the singer, you know, always gets requested. So you'd make quite a bit of money. And they would just keep doing all sorts of things to, you know, make confusion. So finally, I just got disgusted. And I told him I was quitting. And oh, he didn't want me to quit, you know. And Freddie tried to talk to me, but I wouldn't stay. So I had an offer to go to work at the Deluxe for prayer. So right away, I just left and went to work at the Deluxe for prayer. And with Glover Compton. He's a great piano player, too.
